en: The Training Rule on Loud Laughter:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group of six monks were walking through inhabited areas laughing with loud laughter...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not walk through an inhabited area laughing loudly.
One must not walk through an inhabited area laughing loudly."
If one, out of disrespect, goes through an inhabited area laughing a loud laugh, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is absent-minded, one who does not know, or one who is ill.
If he merely smiles at a laughable matter; if it is due to an emergency;
"For one who is a first offender.
The first training rule is concluded.
